newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee rate must be set by market - Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: India rupee rate must be set by market - Chidambaram.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Saturday that the foreign exchange market must determine the value of the rupee.
Chidambaram was asked in an interview with Reuters if there was room for the rupee to depreciate against the U.S. dollar. On Friday the rupee closed at 35.865/870 against the dollar.
"We don't talk of depreciating the rupee or devaluing the rupee," he said. "As I have said, it is the market which must determine the level of the rupee."
Chidambaram said the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) concern was that there should not be volatility in the rupee exchange rate.

Asked if he shared that concern, the finance minister said: "Yes, I share the concern there should not be volatility. The last time there was a high degree of volitility was in, I think, September, November of 1995. That caused problems."
Chidambaram was asked how India could prevent recent large inflows of dollars from stoking inflation. The RBI has recently bought dollars to prevent the rupee from appreciating.
"It all depends on what we do with the dollars. If imports rise, as we expect them to rise and they should rise, then some of these dollars will be consumed. We discuss various options," he said.
Asked if one option would be to relax controls on imports of consumer goods, he said: "I have said it is an option. It is an option, but that has to be decided with the Ex-Im (Export-Import) policy."
The government is due to release a new export-import policy by April 1.

Chidambaram was asked if, as one RBI official recently suggested, India would have to wait until 2000 before the rupee would become fully convertible on the capital account. He said a committee within the RBI would examine the issue.

"Let us see what the road map says. If the road map shows that the journey is short, then we will respond accordingly. If the road map shows that the journey is a long journey, then we will respond accordingly," he said.
The finance minister was asked if it was time to make the rupee fully convertible now that foreign exchange reserves were buoyant and the current account deficit was under control.
"Those are not the only two criteria. There are other criteria," he said.
"The fiscal deficit must be brought under control and above all, inflation must be brought under control. I think there are other criteria before we move to full capital account convertibility."
Chidambaram was asked if a weaker rupee would help boost exports.
"A weaker rupee would help the exporter but a weaker rupee would hurt many others. I don't think we can look at it only from the point of view of the exporter," he said.

The finance minister said world trade had been sluggish. "To some extent that has affected the year's export growth. But I expect imports to pick up this year, as well as exports to pick up," he said.
Asked what time period he was referring to, he said calendar 1997 and the 1997/98 fiscal year starting on April 1.
